body: Hello need some help. DOD delete, RCR Dragmaster cam and all supporting internals with 3600 stall. I have an intermittent RPM surge at idle in park or on the brake in a line or at stop light, sometimes low enough to stall out. But zero issues under throttle or WOT. Cleaned throttle body, replaced MAF, don’t hear any vacuum leak. Any help appreciated.

When they did your tune. Did they raise the base idle rpm? You have the looser converter, they should raise the base idle from 650 to around 750 to keep it from stalling. Or if a lumpy idle was part of the “tune request” they may have messed with the base idle timing to made the idle more lumpy (stupid idea) This could also be part of the stalling. To start, what’s the idle rpm? If you touch the gas lightly to get 800 rpm is it smooth?
This issue did not start till a year or more after the build. She idles around 900 rpm, when the issue isn’t occurring. Once I get into throttle runs flawless.
Likely something has changed to throw off the Base idle airflow if it was doing well when initially tuned. Temps, Elevation, Vacuum Leak or some other unmetered airflow are possibilities.

Is it possible for a tune to alter on its own or like a parameter change somehow? The only point of vacuum I see is a left valve cover. There’s no PCV valve rather the straight through nipple but if I unplugged that hose while it’s running, it seems to smooth out.

The tune's base values will not change. There are some learned idle trims and fuel trims, but they wouldn't be fine for a year and then be out.
Have you added a catch can or valve cover breather or anything? That can allow unmetered air in.

Did not add a catch can or alter any thing under the hood. I have a video clip of it, but don’t know how to attach it in here. I had her idling in the garage for about 20 minutes. Got up to temp cycle. The fans no issue drove 5 miles went into the store came back out on startup has the issue surging. I popped the hood, pulled that tube off the valve cover nipple and a smooth out. I use my finger to plug the tube and the idle dropped surging and wanted to stall.

Having your tuner touch it up could help your surging issue, but typically something physical has to change to go from idling fine for a long period of time to surging.
Was the battery unhooked or dead for a long period of time? That will clear the long term idle trims. If it had learned that it needed to add air to idle smooth and then lost that learned valve, it could take it a while to relearn it. (Ideally it would be tuned close enough that it doesn't have to learn any trims).
